senses.definition_vi: hành động để cân bằng hoặc sửa chữa một cái gì đó sai hoặc không bình thường.

senses.definition: to pay somebody money because they have suffered some damage, loss, injury, etc.

examples.x: Her lawyers say she should be compensated for the suffering she had been caused.

senses.definition_vi: trả tiền cho ai đó vì họ đã phải chịu đựng thiệt hại, mất mát, thương tích, v.v.

senses.definition: something, especially money, that somebody gives you because they have hurt you, or damaged something that you own; the act of giving this to somebody

examples.x: to claim/award/receive compensation
The employer has a duty to pay full compensation for injuries received at work.
to receive £10 000 in compensation
She received a cash sum by way of compensation.

senses.definition_vi: một cái gì đó, đặc biệt là tiền, mà ai đó đưa cho bạn vì họ đã làm tổn thương bạn, hoặc làm hỏng một thứ gì đó bạn sở hữu; hành động đưa cái này cho ai đó.

senses.definition: money that an employee receives for doing their job

examples.x: Send your CV and current compensation to Executive Search Consultant.

senses.definition_vi: tiền mà một nhân viên nhận được khi làm công việc của họ.

senses.definition: a thing or things that make a bad situation better

examples.x: I wish I were young again, but getting older has its compensations.
The grey streets of London were small compensation for the loss of her beloved Africa.

senses.definition_vi: một hoặc nhiều thứ làm cho một tình huống tồi tệ trở nên tốt hơn.

senses.definition: to take part in a contest or game

examples.x: The games were an outstanding success, with almost 2 400 athletes competing.
He's hoping to compete in the London marathon.
Only 21 bodybuilders competed in the event.
They are competing against teams of full-time professional players.
He is expected to compete for the title of world champion next year.

senses.definition_vi: tham gia vào một cuộc thi hoặc trò chơi.

senses.definition: to try to be more successful or better than somebody else who is trying to do the same as you

examples.x: They simply cannot compete in the international market.
Several companies are competing for the contract.
Young children will usually compete for their parents' attention.
The result is more applicants competing for fewer jobs.
Small independent bookshops find it difficult to compete with the online stores.
For too long UK shipyards have been competing against each other.
We can't compete with them on price.
to compete on quality/cost
There are too many magazines competing to attract readers.

senses.definition_vi: cố gắng thành công hơn hoặc tốt hơn người khác đang cố gắng làm điều tương tự như bạn.

senses.definition: the ability to do something well

examples.x: to gain a high level of competence in English
professional/technical competence

senses.definition_vi: khả năng làm điều gì đó tốt.

senses.definition: the power that a court, an organization or a person has to deal with something

examples.x: The judge has to act within the competence of the court.
outside somebody’s area of competence

senses.definition_vi: quyền mà một tòa án, một tổ chức hoặc một người có để giải quyết một vấn đề.

senses.definition: a skill that you need in a particular job or for a particular task

examples.x: The syllabus lists the knowledge and competences required at this level.
You will agree with us a personal learning contract, based on an assessment of personal competences in relation to career objectives.

senses.definition_vi: một kỹ năng bạn cần trong một công việc hoặc nhiệm vụ cụ thể.

senses.definition: having enough skill or knowledge to do something well or to the necessary standard

examples.x: He's very competent in his work.
Make sure the firm is competent to carry out the work.
I don’t feel competent to comment.
She is highly competent at her job.

senses.definition_vi: có đủ kỹ năng hoặc kiến thức để làm điều gì đó tốt hoặc đạt tiêu chuẩn cần thiết

senses.definition: of a good standard but not very good

examples.x: Ron was a competent player—more than that, he was good!

senses.definition_vi: có tiêu chuẩn tốt nhưng không quá xuất sắc

senses.definition: having the power to decide something

examples.x: The case was referred to a competent authority.

senses.definition_vi: có quyền quyết định một vấn đề gì đó

senses.definition: an event in which people compete with each other to find out who is the best at something

examples.x: a design/an art/a talent competition
an international/a national competition
Hundreds of schools entered the competition.
She's won a prestigious singing competition.
He won fourth place in the competition.
a competition to design the new Parliament building

senses.definition_vi: một sự kiện mà mọi người thi đấu với nhau để tìm ra ai giỏi nhất về một thứ gì đó

senses.definition: a situation in which people or organizations compete with each other for something that not everyone can have

examples.x: stiff/fierce/intense/tough competition
competition between two similar products
The government said the new laws would enhance competition among banks.
competition for resources/jobs/food, etc.
competition to secure a place on the course
The firm is facing stiff competition from its online rivals.
Public education is run in direct competition with the private sector.

examples.cf: in competition with somebody/something for something
examples.x: We are in competition with four other companies for the contract.

examples.cf: in competition with somebody/something to do something
examples.x: The programme puts two couples in competition with each other to redecorate one another's homes.

senses.definition_vi: một tình huống mà mọi người hoặc các tổ chức cạnh tranh với nhau để giành lấy thứ mà không phải ai cũng có được

senses.definition: the people who are competing against somebody

examples.x: We'll be able to assess the competition at the conference.
This car consistently outperforms the competition.
The competition is/are bringing out a new model.

senses.definition_vi: những người đang cạnh tranh với ai đó

senses.definition: used to describe a situation in which people or organizations compete against each other

examples.x: competitive games/sports
Graduates have to fight for jobs in an increasingly competitive market.
Those businesses are operating in an extremely competitive environment.
The company has succeeded in a highly competitive industry.

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng để mô tả một tình huống mà mọi người hoặc các tổ chức cạnh tranh với nhau

senses.definition: trying very hard to be better than others

examples.x: You have to be highly competitive to do well in sport these days.

senses.definition_vi: cố gắng rất nhiều để giỏi hơn người khác

senses.definition: as good as or better than others

examples.x: a shop selling clothes at competitive prices (= as low as any other shop)
to gain a competitive advantage over rival companies
How do we maintain our competitive edge?
What is your strategy for helping the company stay competitive in a global market?
We need to work harder to remain competitive with other companies.

senses.definition_vi: tốt bằng hoặc tốt hơn những người khác

senses.definition: a person who takes part in a competition

examples.x: Over 200 competitors entered the race.
the youngest competitor in the event
the most successful South African competitor at the games
There are six remaining competitors for the grand prize of $50 000.

senses.definition_vi: một người tham gia một cuộc thi

senses.definition: a person or an organization that competes against others, especially in business

examples.x: We produce cheaper goods than our competitors.
The company is outperforming its main competitors in the US market.
They are set to become formidable competitors to American companies.
Japan was not a major competitor for scarce resources such as oil.

senses.definition_vi: một người hoặc một tổ chức cạnh tranh với những người khác, đặc biệt là trong kinh doanh

senses.definition: to produce a book, list, report, etc. by bringing together different items, articles, songs, etc.; to collect information in order to produce a book, list, etc.

examples.x: We are trying to compile a list of suitable people for the job.
The album was compiled from live recordings from last year's tour.
The figures were compiled from a survey of 2  000 schoolchildren.

senses.definition_vi: tạo ra một cuốn sách, danh sách, báo cáo, v.v. bằng cách tập hợp các mục, bài báo, bài hát khác nhau; thu thập thông tin để tạo ra một cuốn sách, danh sách, v.v.

senses.definition: to translate instructions from one computer language into another so that a particular computer can understand them
senses.definition_vi: dịch các chỉ dẫn từ ngôn ngữ máy tính này sang ngôn ngữ máy tính khác để một máy tính cụ thể có thể hiểu được

senses.definition: to say that you are annoyed, unhappy or not satisfied about somebody/something

examples.x: She never complains, but she's obviously exhausted.
‘How are you?’ ‘Oh, I can't complain (= I'm all right).’
Annoyed residents have complained to the police.
Shoppers complained about the lack of toilet facilities.
I'm going to complain to the manager about this.
The defendant complained of intimidation during the investigation.
She complained at the unfairness of it all.
He complained bitterly that he had been unfairly treated.
‘It's not fair,’ she complained.

senses.definition_vi: nói rằng bạn khó chịu, không vui hoặc không hài lòng về ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: a reason for not being satisfied; a statement that somebody makes saying that they are not satisfied

examples.x: a formal complaint
She said the police had immediately investigated the complaint.
I'd like to make a complaint about the noise.
to file/lodge (= make) a complaint
The most common complaint is about poor service.
The Tribunal upheld his complaint of discrimination.
I believe you have a complaint against one of our nurses.
They said their complaints to the police were often not acted on.
Council bosses said they would respond to complaints from residents.
We received a number of complaints from customers about the lack of parking facilities.
‘Complaints by patients are now at their lowest level,’ she said.
a complaint that he had been unfairly treated
My only complaint is that the website is a little difficult to use.
We have a clear and effective complaints procedure.

senses.definition_vi: một lý do để không hài lòng; một tuyên bố mà ai đó đưa ra nói rằng họ không hài lòng

senses.definition: the act of complaining

examples.x: I can see no grounds for complaint.
The way I was treated gave me no cause for complaint.
I'm planning to write a formal letter of complaint.
Workers were expected to accept pay cuts without complaint.

senses.definition_vi: hành động phàn nàn

senses.definition: an illness, especially one that is not serious, and often one that affects a particular part of the body

examples.x: He has a minor skin complaint.

senses.definition_vi: một căn bệnh, đặc biệt là một căn bệnh không nghiêm trọng, và thường ảnh hưởng đến một bộ phận cụ thể của cơ thể

senses.definition: to add to something in a way that improves it or makes it more attractive

examples.x: The excellent menu is complemented by a good wine list.
The team needs players who complement each other.
The flavours in the dish complement each other perfectly.

senses.definition_vi: thêm vào một cái gì đó theo cách làm cho nó tốt hơn hoặc hấp dẫn hơn

senses.definition: including all the parts, etc. that are necessary; whole

examples.x: a complete list/sequence/picture/profile
I've collected the complete set.
a complete guide to events in Oxford
the complete works of Shakespeare
You will receive payment for each complete day that you work.
You've made my life complete.
A New Year celebration would not be complete without fireworks.
No trip to Edinburgh would be complete without a visit to the castle.

senses.definition_vi: hoàn thành việc làm hoặc tạo ra một cái gì đó

senses.definition: finished

examples.x: The job is almost complete.
Ther ordering process is nearly complete.
Construction of the new airport is scheduled to be complete by late September.
Work on the office building will be complete at the end of the year.

senses.definition_vi: hoàn thành việc làm hoặc tạo ra một cái gì đó

senses.definition: used when you are emphasizing something, to mean ‘to the greatest degree possible’

examples.x: We were in complete agreement.
Refrigerators brought about a complete change in people's lifestyle.
They sat in complete silence.
He was a complete stranger to me.
The council's response shows a complete lack of understanding of the situation.
The army remains in complete control of the country.
It came as a complete surprise.
I felt a complete idiot.
You are talking complete and utter rubbish.

senses.definition_vi: hoàn thành việc làm hoặc tạo ra một cái gì đó

senses.definition: including something as an extra part or feature

examples.x: The furniture comes complete with tools and instructions for assembly.
The cruise ship is really a floating village, complete with shops, cafes and a doctor's surgery.

senses.definition_vi: hoàn thành việc làm hoặc tạo ra một cái gì đó

senses.definition: in every way possible; in every part

examples.x: It was completely different from how I had imagined it.
I've completely forgotten her name.
The building was completely destroyed by the explosion.
The technique is completely new.
This practice is completely unacceptable.
Remove the cake from the tin and leave to cool completely.
The waiter completely ignored my request.
He should recover completely in time.
I agree completely with what you say.

senses.definition_vi: theo mọi cách có thể; ở mọi bộ phận

senses.definition: the act or process of finishing something; the state of being finished and complete

examples.x: the completion of the new hospital building
Satisfactory completion of the course does not ensure you a job.
The project is due for completion in the spring.
The road is nearing completion (= it is nearly finished).
the date of completion/the completion date

senses.definition_vi: hành động hoặc quá trình hoàn thành một cái gì đó; trạng thái đã hoàn thành và trọn vẹn

senses.definition: the formal act of completing the sale of property, for example the sale of a house

examples.x: The keys will be handed over on completion.
The floorboards were replaced prior to completion of the sale.

senses.definition_vi: hành động chính thức hoàn tất việc bán tài sản, ví dụ như bán nhà

senses.definition: made of many different things or parts that are connected; difficult to understand

examples.x: a complex problem/issue/process/system
a complex argument/subject
complex machinery
the complex structure of the human brain
Scientists need a better understanding of the complex interactions that cause hurricanes to intensify.
We live in an increasingly complex world.
a highly complex situation

senses.definition_vi: một nhóm các tòa nhà cùng loại đặt cùng nhau tại một nơi

senses.definition: containing one main part (= the root of a word or main clause of a sentence) and one or more other parts (called affixes or subordinate clauses)

examples.x: In the complex sentence, ‘I'd like to go to the beach, if it's warm enough’, ‘I'd like to go to the beach’ is the main clause, and ‘if it's warm enough’ is the subordinate clause.

senses.definition_vi: một nhóm các tòa nhà cùng loại đặt cùng nhau tại một nơi

senses.definition: the state of being formed of many parts; the state of being difficult to understand

examples.x: the increasing complexity of modern telecommunication systems
I was astonished by the size and complexity of the problem.

senses.definition_vi: trạng thái được tạo thành từ nhiều bộ phận; trạng thái khó hiểu

senses.definition: the features of a problem or situation that are difficult to understand

examples.x: the complexities of the system

senses.definition_vi: các đặc điểm của một vấn đề hoặc tình huống khó hiểu

senses.definition: the practice of obeying rules or requests made by people in authority

examples.x: procedures that must be followed to ensure full compliance with the law
Safety measures were carried out in compliance with paragraph 6 of the building regulations.
The compliance officer is responsible for enforcing policies and procedures.

senses.definition_vi: thực hành tuân theo các quy tắc hoặc yêu cầu do những người có thẩm quyền đưa ra

senses.definition: the quality of being too willing to agree with somebody or do what they want

examples.x: He was appalled by his parents' unquestioning compliance with the regime.

senses.definition_vi: phẩm chất quá sẵn lòng đồng ý với ai đó hoặc làm những gì họ muốn

senses.definition: made of many different things or parts that are connected; difficult to understand

examples.x: a complicated issue/process/system
The instructions look very complicated.
The story is extremely complicated.
It's all very complicated—but I'll try and explain.
Things get complicated when the hero becomes the target of a stalker.
Life had become more complicated for them.
Some of the maths questions were far too complicated for your average 10-year-old.

senses.definition_vi: được tạo thành từ nhiều thứ hoặc bộ phận khác nhau được kết nối; khó hiểu

senses.definition: a thing that makes a situation more complicated or difficult

examples.x: The bad weather added a further complication to our journey.

senses.definition_vi: một điều làm cho tình huống trở nên phức tạp hoặc khó khăn hơn

senses.definition: a new problem or illness that makes treatment of a previous one more complicated or difficult

examples.x: She developed complications after the surgery.
Infertility is one of the complications of this type of radiotherapy.

senses.definition_vi: một vấn đề hoặc bệnh mới làm cho việc điều trị một vấn đề trước đó trở nên phức tạp hoặc khó khăn hơn

senses.definition: to obey a rule, an order, etc.; to meet particular standards

examples.x: They refused to comply with the UN resolution.
All furniture must comply with the fire safety regulations.
When requested to leave, they refused to comply.
What sanctions can they take against us if we fail to comply?

senses.definition_vi: tuân theo một quy tắc, một mệnh lệnh, v.v.; đáp ứng các tiêu chuẩn cụ thể

senses.definition: one of several parts of which something is made

examples.x: the different organizations involved in the design of the various components
Key components of the government’s plan are…
an essential/important component of something
a major/principal/critical component of something
Nitrogen is the main component of air.
The country still lacks the basic components of a real democratic system.
the components of a machine
Individual components for the car can be very expensive.
Trust is a vital component in any relationship.
Component failure was the cause of the accident.

senses.definition_vi: một trong nhiều bộ phận tạo nên một thứ gì đó

senses.definition: to write music

examples.x: Mozart composed his last opera shortly before he died.
music specially composed for the occasion

senses.definition_vi: viết nhạc

senses.definition: to write a letter, etc. usually with a lot of care and thought

examples.x: She composed a letter of protest.

senses.definition_vi: viết một lá thư, v.v., thường với nhiều sự cẩn thận và suy nghĩ

senses.definition: to combine together to form a whole

examples.x: Ten people compose the committee.

senses.definition_vi: kết hợp lại để tạo thành một tổng thể

senses.definition: to manage to control your feelings or expression

examples.x: Emma frowned, making an effort to compose herself.
I was so confused that I could hardly compose my thoughts.

senses.definition_vi: cố gắng kiểm soát cảm xúc hoặc biểu hiện của bạn

senses.definition: a person who writes music, especially classical music

examples.x: Verdi was a prolific composer of operas.

senses.definition_vi: một người viết nhạc, đặc biệt là nhạc cổ điển

senses.definition: the different parts that something is made of; the way in which the different parts are organized

examples.x: the chemical composition of the soil
the composition of the board of directors
the size and composition of an average class

senses.definition_vi: các bộ phận khác nhau tạo nên một thứ gì đó; cách các bộ phận khác nhau được tổ chức

senses.definition: a short text that is written as a school exercise; a short essay

examples.x: a composition on the effects of crime
In the exam you will have to do a composition.

senses.definition_vi: một đoạn văn ngắn được viết như một bài tập ở trường; một bài luận ngắn

senses.definition: a piece of music or art, or a poem

examples.x: one of Beethoven’s finest compositions

senses.definition_vi: một bản nhạc, tác phẩm nghệ thuật hoặc một bài thơ

senses.definition: the act of composing something, especially a piece of music; the art of writing music

examples.x: pieces performed in the order of their composition
to study composition

senses.definition_vi: hành động sáng tác một cái gì đó, đặc biệt là một bản nhạc; nghệ thuật viết nhạc

senses.definition: the arrangement of people or objects in a painting or photograph
senses.definition_vi: sự sắp xếp người hoặc vật trong một bức tranh hoặc ảnh

senses.definition: a thing consisting of two or more separate things combined together

examples.x: compounds derived from rainforest plants
The air smelled like a compound of diesel and petrol fumes.

senses.definition_vi: một thứ bao gồm hai hoặc nhiều thứ riêng biệt kết hợp với nhau

senses.definition: a substance formed by a chemical reaction of two or more elements in fixed amounts relative to each other

examples.x: Common salt is a compound of sodium and chlorine.

senses.definition_vi: một chất được hình thành bởi phản ứng hóa học của hai hoặc nhiều nguyên tố với số lượng cố định tương đối với nhau

senses.definition: a noun, an adjective or a verb made of two or more words or parts of words, written as one or more words, or joined by a hyphen. Travel agent, dark-haired and bathroom are all compounds.

examples.x: Most compound nouns form their plurals in the usual way.

senses.definition_vi: một danh từ, tính từ hoặc động từ được tạo thành từ hai hoặc nhiều từ hoặc bộ phận của từ, được viết thành một hoặc nhiều từ, hoặc được nối bằng dấu gạch nối. Travel agent, dark-haired và bathroom đều là từ ghép.

senses.definition: an area surrounded by a fence or wall in which a factory or other group of buildings stands

examples.x: life inside the prison compound

senses.definition_vi: một khu vực được bao quanh bởi hàng rào hoặc tường nơi có nhà máy hoặc một nhóm tòa nhà khác

senses.definition: including all, or almost all, the items, details, facts, information, etc., that may be involved

examples.x: a comprehensive list of addresses
a comprehensive study
comprehensive insurance (= covering all risks)

senses.definition_vi: bao gồm tất cả, hoặc gần như tất cả, các mục, chi tiết, sự kiện, thông tin, v.v., có thể liên quan

senses.definition: designed for students of all abilities in the same school
senses.definition_vi: được thiết kế cho học sinh có năng lực khác nhau trong cùng một trường

senses.definition: gained or lost by a large amount

examples.x: The cricket team finished the season with a comprehensive victory over their rivals.

senses.definition_vi: đạt được hoặc mất đi với số lượng lớn

senses.definition: to have somebody/something as parts or members

examples.x: The collection comprises 327 paintings.
a book comprising eight short stories
The committee is comprised of representatives from both the public and private sectors.

senses.definition_vi: có người/thứ gì đó làm các bộ phận hoặc thành viên

senses.definition: to be the parts or members that form something

examples.x: Older people comprise a large proportion of those living in poverty.

senses.definition_vi: là các bộ phận hoặc thành viên tạo nên một thứ gì đó

senses.definition: an agreement made between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end

examples.x: After lengthy talks the two sides finally reached a compromise.
In any relationship, you have to make compromises.
a compromise solution/agreement/candidate

senses.definition_vi: từ bỏ một số yêu cầu của bạn để đạt được thỏa thuận sau khi bất đồng với ai đó

senses.definition: a solution to a problem in which two or more things cannot exist together as they are, in which each thing is reduced or changed slightly so that they can exist together

examples.x: This model represents the best compromise between price and quality.
It was a fair compromise between the two sides.

senses.definition_vi: từ bỏ một số yêu cầu của bạn để đạt được thỏa thuận sau khi bất đồng với ai đó

senses.definition: the act of reaching a compromise

examples.x: Compromise is an inevitable part of life.
There is no prospect of compromise in sight.
There could be no compromise with the nationalists.

senses.definition_vi: từ bỏ một số yêu cầu của bạn để đạt được thỏa thuận sau khi bất đồng với ai đó

senses.definition: that must be done because of a law or a rule

examples.x: English is a compulsory subject at this level.
compulsory education/schooling
The strikers are protesting against the threat of compulsory redundancies.

examples.cf: it is compulsory (for somebody/something) to do something
examples.x: It is compulsory for all motorcyclists to wear helmets.

senses.definition_vi: phải làm vì luật hoặc quy tắc

senses.definition: to calculate something

examples.x: The losses were computed at £5 million.
These measurements can be used to compute the average size.

senses.definition_vi: tính toán một cái gì đó

senses.definition: to make sense

examples.x: That just doesn't compute.

senses.definition_vi: có ý nghĩa

senses.definition: an electronic machine that can store, organize and find information, do processes with numbers and other data, and control other machines

examples.x: a home computer
The whole process is run and monitored by computer.
He spends all day playing on his computer.
a computer system/program/network
computer software/graphics/hardware
a computer screen
a computer programmer/user
a computer virus
computer-aided design

senses.definition_vi: một máy điện tử có thể lưu trữ, tổ chức và tìm kiếm thông tin, thực hiện các quy trình với số và dữ liệu khác, và điều khiển các máy khác

senses.definition: to hide somebody/something

examples.x: The paintings were concealed beneath a thick layer of plaster.
Tim could barely conceal his disappointment.
She sat down to conceal the fact that she was trembling.
For a long time his death was concealed from her.

senses.definition_vi: giấu ai đó/thứ gì đó

senses.definition: to admit that something is true, logical, etc. after first denying it or resisting it

examples.x: ‘Not bad,’ she conceded grudgingly.
He was forced to concede (that) there might be difficulties.
I had to concede the logic of this.
He reluctantly conceded the point to me.
He reluctantly conceded me the point.
It must be conceded that different judges have different approaches to these cases.

senses.definition_vi: thừa nhận rằng điều gì đó là đúng, hợp lý, v.v. sau khi ban đầu phủ nhận hoặc chống lại nó

senses.definition: to admit that you have lost a game, an election, etc.

examples.x: After losing this decisive battle, the general was forced to concede.
Injury forced Hicks to concede defeat.

senses.definition_vi: thừa nhận rằng bạn đã thua một trận đấu, một cuộc bầu cử, v.v.

senses.definition: to give something away, especially unwillingly; to allow somebody to have something

examples.x: The president was obliged to concede power to the army.
England conceded a goal immediately after half-time.
Women were only conceded full voting rights in the 1950s.
The firm should concede a significant salary increase to its employees.

senses.definition_vi: nhượng lại một cái gì đó, đặc biệt là không tự nguyện; cho phép ai đó có được thứ gì đó

senses.definition: to form an idea, a plan, etc. in your mind

examples.x: He conceived the idea of transforming the old power station into an arts centre.
The dam project was originally conceived in 1997.

senses.definition_vi: hình thành một ý tưởng, một kế hoạch, v.v. trong tâm trí bạn

senses.definition: to imagine something

examples.x: God is often conceived of as male.
I cannot conceive (= I do not believe) (that) he would wish to harm us.
I cannot conceive what it must be like.

senses.definition_vi: tưởng tượng một cái gì đó

senses.definition: when a woman conceives or conceives a child, she becomes pregnant

examples.x: She is unable to conceive.
Their first child was conceived on their wedding night.
She was unable to conceive a child naturally and was offered fertility treatment.

senses.definition_vi: khi một phụ nữ thụ thai hoặc thụ thai một đứa trẻ, cô ấy mang thai

senses.definition: to give all your attention to something and not think about anything else

examples.x: I can't concentrate with all that noise going on.
I struggled to concentrate on my job because I was worried about my son.
He tried to concentrate on reading his book but couldn't.
Nothing concentrates the mind better than the knowledge that you could die tomorrow (= it makes you think very clearly).
After 1926 she concentrated her energies on her medical practice.
I decided to concentrate all my efforts on finding somewhere to live.

senses.definition_vi: dồn toàn bộ sự chú ý của bạn vào một việc gì đó và không nghĩ về bất cứ điều gì khác

senses.definition: to bring something together in one place

examples.x: Power is largely concentrated in the hands of a small elite.
We need to concentrate resources on the most run-down areas.
Fighting was concentrated around the towns to the north.
Never concentrate the heat in one place for too long.

senses.definition_vi: mang một cái gì đó lại với nhau ở một nơi

senses.definition: to increase the strength of a substance by reducing its volume, for example by boiling it
senses.definition_vi: tăng cường độ của một chất bằng cách giảm thể tích của nó, ví dụ bằng cách đun sôi

senses.definition: the ability to direct all your effort and attention on one thing, without thinking of other things

examples.x: This book requires a great deal of concentration.
Tiredness affects your powers of concentration.
One momentary lapse in concentration could prove fatal.
He has a poor concentration span (= cannot concentrate for long).

senses.definition_vi: khả năng dồn toàn bộ nỗ lực và sự chú ý của bạn vào một việc, mà không nghĩ đến những việc khác

senses.definition: the process of people directing effort and attention on a particular thing

examples.x: He stressed the need for greater concentration on environmental issues.
In his concentration on the job in hand, John allowed his normal vigilance to slip.

senses.definition_vi: quá trình mọi người dồn nỗ lực và sự chú ý vào một việc cụ thể

senses.definition: a lot of something in one place

examples.x: a concentration of industry in the north of the country

senses.definition_vi: một lượng lớn của một cái gì đó ở một nơi

senses.definition: the amount of a substance in a liquid or in another substance

examples.x: glucose concentrations in the blood

senses.definition_vi: lượng một chất trong một chất lỏng hoặc trong một chất khác

senses.definition: an idea or a principle that is connected with something abstract

examples.x: the concept of social class
helping students grasp abstract concepts such as leadership and teamwork
basic/fundamental/key/core concepts
the concept that everyone should have equality of opportunity
the concepts behind an artist's work

senses.definition_vi: một ý tưởng hoặc một nguyên tắc có liên quan đến một cái gì đó trừu tượng

senses.definition: an idea for something new

examples.x: a novel/innovative concept
an exciting new concept in city living
a novel marketing concept
a design concept for a new school

senses.definition_vi: một ý tưởng cho một cái gì đó mới

senses.definition: an understanding or a belief of what something/somebody is or what something/somebody should be

examples.x: Marx’s conception of social justice
He has no conception of how difficult life is if you're unemployed.
I had to reassess my conception that she was basically an honest person.

senses.definition_vi: sự hiểu biết hoặc niềm tin về một người/vật là gì hoặc một người/vật nên như thế nào

senses.definition: the process of forming an idea or a plan

examples.x: The plan was brilliant in its conception but failed because of lack of money.

senses.definition_vi: quá trình hình thành một ý tưởng hoặc một kế hoạch

senses.definition: the process of an egg being fertilized inside a woman’s body so that she becomes pregnant

examples.x: the moment of conception
A child is born about 40 weeks after conception takes place.

senses.definition_vi: quá trình trứng được thụ tinh bên trong cơ thể phụ nữ để cô ấy mang thai

senses.definition: a feeling of worry, especially one that is shared by many people

examples.x: Villagers expressed concern about the level of traffic.
There is growing concern about the increase in deforestation.
The report raises serious concerns over safety at the plant.
She hasn't been seen for four days and there is concern for her safety.
to raise/voice concerns
We are trying to address the concerns of residents.
Don't hesitate to ask if you have any questions or concerns.
The school's recent examination results have sparked concern among parents.
There is widespread concern that new houses will be built on protected land.
security/safety concerns
He had to resign from his job because of health concerns.
The president's health was giving serious cause for concern.
The continuing drought is causing concern among farmers.
This is a matter of grave concern to our members.
We view these developments with concern.
The cost of the scheme is of major concern.

senses.definition_vi: ảnh hưởng đến ai đó/điều gì đó; liên quan đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: a desire to protect and help somebody/something

examples.x: parents’ concern for their children
deep/genuine/real concern
He showed deep concern for his employees.
She forgot her own worries in her concern for him.
I appreciate everyone's concern and help at this difficult time.

senses.definition_vi: ảnh hưởng đến ai đó/điều gì đó; liên quan đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: something that is important to a person, an organization, etc.

examples.x: Our main concern is to ensure the safety of the children.
What are your biggest concerns as a writer?
The government's primary concern is to reduce crime.
a big/major concern

senses.definition_vi: ảnh hưởng đến ai đó/điều gì đó; liên quan đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: something that is your responsibility or that you have a right to know about

examples.x: This matter is their concern.
How much money I make is none of your concern.
How much we paid is none of your concern.

senses.definition_vi: ảnh hưởng đến ai đó/điều gì đó; liên quan đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: a company or business

examples.x: The scheme has been set up by a major publishing concern.
a successful publishing concern

senses.definition_vi: ảnh hưởng đến ai đó/điều gì đó; liên quan đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: a business or an activity that is making a profit and is expected to continue to do well

examples.x: He sold the cafe as a going concern.
They knew that, as a going concern, the cafe would command a higher price with prospective buyers.

senses.definition_vi: ảnh hưởng đến ai đó/điều gì đó; liên quan đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: worried and feeling concern about something/somebody

examples.x: Concerned citizens can have a huge impact.
concerned parents/residents/parents/locals
The president is deeply concerned about this issue.
We are extremely concerned about her.
He didn't seem in the least concerned for her safety.
We were concerned for his welfare.
I told him but he didn't seem overly concerned (= he was not very concerned)
She was concerned that she might miss the turning and get lost.
Local residents are concerned over the impact of the project.
I was rather concerned at the severity of the punishment.
Her parents are growing increasingly concerned by her erratic behaviour.
a concerned look/glance

senses.definition_vi: lo lắng và cảm thấy bận tâm về điều gì đó/ai đó

senses.definition: affected by something; involved in something

examples.x: The loss was a tragedy for all concerned.
Where our children's education is concerned, no compromise is acceptable.
The individuals concerned have some explaining to do.
The meetings were often embarrassing for all concerned.
Everyone who was directly concerned in (= had some responsibility for) the incident has now resigned.

senses.definition_vi: bị ảnh hưởng bởi điều gì đó; liên quan đến điều gì đó

senses.definition: interested in something; dealing with something

examples.x: The public is increasingly concerned with how food is produced.
Mathematics is concerned essentially with understanding abstract concepts.

senses.definition_vi: quan tâm đến điều gì đó; xử lý điều gì đó

senses.definition: to think it is important to do something

examples.x: She was concerned to write about situations that everybody could identify with.

senses.definition_vi: cho rằng điều gì đó quan trọng cần phải làm

senses.definition: used to give your personal opinion on something

examples.x: As far as I am concerned, you can do what you like.

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng để đưa ra ý kiến cá nhân của bạn về một điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to give facts or an opinion about a particular aspect of something

examples.x: She's doing fine as far as French is concerned, it's her German I'm worried about.

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng để đưa ra các sự kiện hoặc ý kiến về một khía cạnh cụ thể của một điều gì đó

senses.definition: a public performance of music

examples.x: to attend/go to a concert
The orchestra gave a concert in Miami in January.
a series of concerts organized by the Oxford Chamber Music Society
a classical/rock/pop concert
a benefit/charity concert
They're in concert at Wembley arena.
They also performed at a concert in Rome last month.
a concert of music by Bach
I got dragged along to concerts by bands I hated.
a fundraising concert for tsunami victims
a concert hall
a concert pianist/tour/series

senses.definition_vi: một buổi biểu diễn âm nhạc công cộng

senses.definition: working together with somebody/something
senses.definition_vi: làm việc cùng nhau với ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: something that you allow or do, or allow somebody to have, in order to end an argument or to make a situation less difficult

examples.x: The firm will be forced to make concessions if it wants to avoid a strike.
to win a concession from somebody
a major/an important concession
She made no concession to his inexperience as a manager.

senses.definition_vi: điều gì đó bạn cho phép hoặc làm, hoặc cho phép ai đó có, để chấm dứt một cuộc tranh cãi hoặc làm cho tình huống bớt khó khăn

senses.definition: the act of giving something or allowing something; the act of conceding

examples.x: the concession of university status to some colleges
her concession speech (= when she admitted that she had lost the election)
Military support was offered in return for the concession of territory.

senses.definition_vi: hành động nhượng bộ hoặc cho phép điều gì đó; hành động thừa nhận

senses.definition: a reduction in an amount of money that has to be paid; a ticket that is sold at a reduced price to a particular group of people

examples.x: They may grant tax concessions to encourage foreign investors.
Tickets are £3; there is a £1 concession for students.
Adults £2.50, concessions £2, family £5
Travel concessions are available to older people.

senses.definition_vi: sự giảm số tiền phải trả; vé được bán với giá giảm cho một nhóm người cụ thể

senses.definition: a right or an advantage that is given to a group of people, an organization, etc., especially by a government or an employer

examples.x: The Bolivian government has granted logging concessions covering 22 million hectares.
The company has just won a mining concession in the north of the country.

senses.definition_vi: quyền hoặc lợi ích được trao cho một nhóm người, một tổ chức, v.v., đặc biệt là bởi chính phủ hoặc người sử dụng lao động

senses.definition: the right to sell something in a particular place; the place where you sell it, sometimes an area that is part of a larger building or store

examples.x: the burger concessions at the stadium
They went to the concession stand to get a hot dog.

senses.definition_vi: quyền bán một cái gì đó ở một địa điểm cụ thể; nơi bạn bán nó, đôi khi là một khu vực là một phần của một tòa nhà hoặc cửa hàng lớn hơn

senses.definition: to decide or believe something as a result of what you have heard or seen

examples.x: It is too early for us to conclude anything.
What do you conclude from that?
The report concluded (that) the cheapest option was to close the laboratory.
He concluded from their remarks that they were not in favour of the plan.
It was concluded that the level of change necessary would be low.
‘So it should be safe to continue,’ he concluded.

senses.definition_vi: quyết định hoặc tin vào điều gì đó như là kết quả của những gì bạn đã nghe hoặc thấy

senses.definition: to come to an end; to bring something to an end

examples.x: This was how the negotiations finally concluded.
Let me make just a few concluding remarks.
the concluding chapter of the book
The programme concluded with Stravinsky's ‘Rite of Spring’.
He concluded by wishing everyone a safe trip home.
The commission concluded its investigation last month.
And that concludes our programme for today.
The main responsibility of a salesperson is to conclude a sale successfully.
She concluded her speech with a quotation from Shakespeare.
‘Anyway, she should be back soon,’ he concluded.

senses.definition_vi: chấm dứt; mang một cái gì đó đến hồi kết

senses.definition: to arrange and settle an agreement with somebody formally and finally

examples.x: They concluded a treaty with Turkey.
A trade agreement was concluded between the two countries.
The problems arose from the failure to conclude a new agreement.

senses.definition_vi: sắp xếp và giải quyết một thỏa thuận với ai đó một cách chính thức và cuối cùng

senses.definition: something that you decide when you have thought about all the information connected with the situation

examples.x: We can safely draw some conclusions from our discussion.
He arrived at a different conclusion.
There is abundant evidence to support this conclusion.
Other studies have yielded the same conclusion.
The final section summarizes the conclusions of the study.
I've come to the conclusion that he's not the right person for the job.
New evidence might lead to the conclusion that we are wrong.
It is too soon to reach any conclusions about voting trends.

senses.definition_vi: điều bạn quyết định khi bạn đã suy nghĩ về tất cả thông tin liên quan đến tình huống

senses.definition: the end of something such as a speech or a piece of writing

examples.x: The conclusion of the book was disappointing.
After his death, his assistant completed chapters nine and ten and wrote the conclusion.
If we took this argument to its logical conclusion…
The film is a fitting conclusion to the series.
In conclusion (= finally), I would like to thank…

senses.definition_vi: sự kết thúc của một cái gì đó như một bài phát biểu hoặc một bài viết

senses.definition: the formal and final arrangement of something official

examples.x: the successful conclusion of a trade treaty

senses.definition_vi: sự sắp xếp chính thức và cuối cùng của một điều gì đó có tính chất công vụ.

senses.definition: if you say that something is a foregone conclusion, you mean that it is a result that is certain to happen

examples.x: The outcome of the vote is a foregone conclusion.
The result of the game was a foregone conclusion.

senses.definition_vi: nếu bạn nói rằng điều gì đó là một kết quả đã được định trước, bạn có nghĩa là đó là một kết quả chắc chắn sẽ xảy ra.

senses.definition: to make a decision about somebody/something too quickly, before you know or have thought about all the facts

examples.x: There I go again—jumping to conclusions.

senses.definition_vi: đưa ra quyết định về ai đó/điều gì đó quá nhanh, trước khi bạn biết hoặc đã suy nghĩ về tất cả các sự kiện.

senses.definition: made of concrete

examples.x: a concrete floor

senses.definition_vi: vật liệu xây dựng được tạo ra bằng cách trộn xi măng, cát, đá nhỏ và nước.

senses.definition: based on facts, not on ideas or guesses

examples.x: concrete evidence/proposals/proof
‘It's only a suspicion,’ she said, ‘nothing concrete.’
It is easier to think in concrete terms rather than in the abstract.

senses.definition_vi: vật liệu xây dựng được tạo ra bằng cách trộn xi măng, cát, đá nhỏ và nước.

senses.definition: a concrete object is one that you can see and feel
senses.definition_vi: vật liệu xây dựng được tạo ra bằng cách trộn xi măng, cát, đá nhỏ và nước.

senses.definition: to say very strongly that you think something is bad, usually for moral reasons

examples.x: The government issued a statement condemning the killings.
The editor of the newspaper was condemned as lacking integrity.

senses.definition_vi: nói rất mạnh mẽ rằng bạn nghĩ điều gì đó là xấu, thường vì lý do đạo đức.

senses.definition: to say what somebody’s punishment will be

examples.x: He was condemned to death for murder and later hanged.
She was condemned to hang for killing her husband.

senses.definition_vi: nói về hình phạt của ai đó.

senses.definition: to force somebody to accept a difficult or unpleasant situation

examples.x: He was condemned to a life of hardship.
They were condemned to spend every holiday on a rainy campsite.

senses.definition_vi: buộc ai đó phải chấp nhận một tình huống khó khăn hoặc khó chịu.

senses.definition: to say officially that something is not safe enough to be used

examples.x: The meat was condemned as unfit to eat.
a condemned building

senses.definition_vi: chính thức tuyên bố rằng một cái gì đó không đủ an toàn để sử dụng.

senses.definition: to show or suggest that somebody is guilty of something

examples.x: She is condemned out of her own mouth (= her own words show that she is guilty).

senses.definition_vi: chỉ ra hoặc gợi ý rằng ai đó có tội về điều gì đó.

senses.definition: the state that something is in

examples.x: to be in pristine/excellent/perfect condition
Many of the paintings are in poor condition.
The condition of the roads is poor.

senses.definition_vi: trạng thái của một cái gì đó.

senses.definition: the state of somebody’s health or how fit they are

examples.x: He is overweight and out of condition (= not physically fit).
The motorcyclist was in a critical condition (= at risk of dying) in hospital last night.
in a stable/serious condition
You are in no condition (= too ill/sick, etc.) to go anywhere.
She shouldn't be smoking in her condition (= because she is pregnant).
Her condition has deteriorated.

senses.definition_vi: tình trạng sức khỏe của ai đó hoặc mức độ thể lực của họ.

senses.definition: an illness or a medical problem that you have for a long time because it is not possible to cure it

examples.x: Does your child have any kind of medical condition that we should know about?
She has a serious health condition.
a heart/skin condition
He suffers from a serious heart condition.
The drug is used to treat conditions such as epilepsy.

senses.definition_vi: một căn bệnh hoặc một vấn đề y tế mà bạn mắc phải trong một thời gian dài vì không thể chữa khỏi.

senses.definition: the circumstances or situation in which people live, work or do things

examples.x: working/living conditions
economic/market conditions
They were working under appalling conditions.
a strike over pay and conditions
to improve conditions for workers
He grew up in conditions of poverty.

senses.definition_vi: các hoàn cảnh hoặc tình huống mà mọi người sống, làm việc hoặc làm những việc.

senses.definition: the physical situation that affects how something happens

examples.x: The plants grow best in cool, damp conditions.
The boat sank in adverse weather conditions.
dry/wet/harsh conditions
Studies show that the drug may be harmful under certain conditions.
extreme environmental conditions
treacherous driving conditions
Conditions are ideal for sailing today.

senses.definition_vi: tình trạng vật lý ảnh hưởng đến cách một điều gì đó xảy ra.

senses.definition: a rule or decision that you must agree to, sometimes forming part of a contract or an official agreement

examples.x: The offer is subject to certain conditions.
They agreed to lend us the car on condition that (= only if) we returned it before the weekend.
The officials spoke on condition of anonymity.
They will give us the money on one condition—that we pay it back within six months.
They agreed under the condition that the matter be dealt with promptly.
Congress can impose strict conditions on the bank.
to satisfy/meet/fulfill a condition
They have agreed to a ceasefire provided their conditions are met.

senses.definition_vi: một quy tắc hoặc quyết định mà bạn phải đồng ý, đôi khi là một phần của hợp đồng hoặc thỏa thuận chính thức.

senses.definition: a situation that must exist in order for something else to happen

examples.x: Stable political leadership is a necessary condition for economic growth.
conditions for investment/success/development
We are working to create the conditions for peace.
Applicants must agree to teach for three years as a condition of admission to the program.

examples.cf: as a condition of doing something
examples.x: You can't make a consumer buy something as a condition of getting a loan.

senses.definition_vi: một tình huống phải tồn tại để một điều gì đó khác có thể xảy ra.

senses.definition: the state of a particular group of people because of their situation in life, their problems, etc.

examples.x: He spoke angrily about the condition of the urban poor.
Work is basic to the human condition (= the fact of being alive).
We are aiming to improve the condition of the urban poor.

senses.definition_vi: tình trạng của một nhóm người cụ thể do tình hình cuộc sống, các vấn đề của họ, v.v.

senses.definition: new or as good as new; in perfect condition

examples.x: We sell first editions of rare books in mint condition.

senses.definition_vi: mới hoặc tốt như mới; trong tình trạng hoàn hảo.

senses.definition: not in any situation; never

examples.x: You must on no condition tell them what happened.

senses.definition_vi: không ở trong bất kỳ tình huống nào; không bao giờ.

senses.definition: a person’s behaviour in a particular place or in a particular situation

examples.x: The sport has a strict code of conduct.
improving standards of training and professional conduct
Any allegation of criminal conduct has to be taken seriously.
a complaint about the conduct of a police officer
The United player was fined £5 000 for improper conduct towards an official.

senses.definition_vi: tổ chức và/hoặc thực hiện một hoạt động cụ thể.

senses.definition: the way in which a business or an activity is organized and managed

examples.x: There was growing criticism of the government's conduct of the war.

senses.definition_vi: tổ chức và/hoặc thực hiện một hoạt động cụ thể.

senses.definition: to discuss something with somebody, in order to exchange opinions or get advice

examples.x: He wanted to confer with his colleagues before reaching a decision.

senses.definition_vi: thảo luận một điều gì đó với ai đó, để trao đổi ý kiến hoặc nhận lời khuyên.

senses.definition: to give somebody an award, a university degree or a particular honour or right

examples.x: An honorary degree was conferred on him by Oxford University in 2019.

senses.definition_vi: trao cho ai đó một giải thưởng, bằng đại học hoặc một danh hiệu hoặc quyền lợi cụ thể.

senses.definition: a large official meeting, usually lasting for a few days, at which people with the same work or interests come together to discuss their views

examples.x: The hotel is used for exhibitions, conferences and social events.
to host/organize a conference
to speak at/address a conference
The conference will be held in Glasgow.
Delegates to the Labour Party's annual conference will be staying in the Grand Hotel.
the national conference of the American Psychiatric Association
We met at an international conference.
The resolution will be debated at the party conference in Brighton.
She is attending a three-day conference on climate change.
a conference for health professionals from around the world
a conference room/centre

senses.definition_vi: một cuộc họp chính thức lớn, thường kéo dài vài ngày, tại đó những người có cùng công việc hoặc sở thích gặp nhau để thảo luận về quan điểm của họ.

senses.definition: a meeting at which people have formal discussions

examples.x: They agreed to convene a peace conference by mid-November.
Her working day consists of conferences with foreign diplomats.
He was in conference with his lawyers all day.
Ministers from all four countries involved will meet at the conference table this week.

senses.definition_vi: một cuộc họp mà mọi người có các cuộc thảo luận chính thức.

senses.definition: a group of sports teams that play against each other in a league

examples.x: Southeast Conference football champions

senses.definition_vi: một nhóm các đội thể thao thi đấu với nhau trong một giải đấu.

senses.definition: to admit, especially formally or to the police, that you have done something wrong or illegal

examples.x: After hours of questioning, the suspect confessed.
She confessed to the murder.
He confessed that he had stolen the money.
She confessed to me that she had known his true identity for some time.
We persuaded her to confess her crime.

senses.definition_vi: thừa nhận, đặc biệt là chính thức hoặc với cảnh sát, rằng bạn đã làm điều gì đó sai trái hoặc bất hợp pháp.

senses.definition: to admit something that you feel ashamed or embarrassed about

examples.x: She was reluctant to confess her ignorance.
I must confess to knowing nothing about golf.
I confess (that) I know nothing about golf.
‘I know nothing about it,’ he confessed.
I confess myself bewildered by their explanation.

senses.definition_vi: thừa nhận điều gì đó mà bạn cảm thấy xấu hổ hoặc bối rối.

senses.definition: to tell God or a priest about the bad things you have done so that you can say that you are sorry and be forgiven

examples.x: They had confessed their sins and done their penance.

senses.definition_vi: nói với Chúa hoặc linh mục về những điều xấu bạn đã làm để bạn có thể nói rằng bạn xin lỗi và được tha thứ.

senses.definition: to hear somebody confess their sins (= the bad things they have done)
senses.definition_vi: nghe ai đó thú nhận tội lỗi của họ (= những điều xấu họ đã làm).

senses.definition: a statement that a person makes, admitting that they are guilty of a crime; the act of making such a statement

examples.x: After hours of questioning by police, she made a full confession.
His confession was extracted under torture.

senses.definition_vi: một lời tuyên bố mà một người đưa ra, thừa nhận rằng họ có tội trong một vụ án hình sự; hành động đưa ra lời tuyên bố như vậy.

senses.definition: a statement admitting something that you are ashamed or embarrassed about; the act of making such a statement

examples.x: I've a confession to make—I lied about my age.

senses.definition_vi: một lời tuyên bố thừa nhận điều gì đó mà bạn cảm thấy xấu hổ hoặc bối rối; hành động đưa ra lời tuyên bố như vậy.

senses.definition: a private statement to a priest about the bad things that you have done; an occasion when you make such a statement

examples.x: The priest heard her confession and granted absolution.
I used to go to confession every Saturday as a child.

senses.definition_vi: một lời tuyên bố riêng tư với một linh mục về những điều tồi tệ mà bạn đã làm; một dịp mà bạn đưa ra một tuyên bố như vậy

senses.definition: a statement of your religious beliefs, principles, etc.

examples.x: a confession of faith

senses.definition_vi: một lời tuyên bố về niềm tin tôn giáo, nguyên tắc, v.v. của bạn

senses.definition: the feeling that you can trust, believe in and be sure about the abilities or good qualities of somebody/something

examples.x: The president's actions hardly inspire confidence.
The players all have confidence in their manager.
He believes his reforms will restore confidence in the financial markets.
The survey revealed a lack of confidence in the government.
She has the utmost confidence in her students' abilities.
Our aim is to increase public confidence in the democratic process.
The university is facing a crisis of confidence about its future role.
The new contracts have undermined the confidence of employees.

senses.definition_vi: cảm giác rằng bạn có thể tin tưởng, tin vào và chắc chắn về khả năng hoặc phẩm chất tốt của ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: a belief in your own ability to do things and be successful

examples.x: People often lose confidence when they are criticized.
He gained confidence when he went to college.
Receiving compliments from my work colleagues has boosted my confidence.
The course will help you build your confidence and develop your study skills.
She certainly doesn't lack confidence.
He suffers from a lack of confidence.
She answered the questions with confidence.
I didn't have any confidence in myself at school.
Winning the award has given me much more confidence in my writing.
The training programmes have given workers the confidence to take on more responsibility.

senses.definition_vi: niềm tin vào khả năng của chính bạn để làm mọi việc và thành công

senses.definition: the feeling that you are certain about something

examples.x: He said he wished that he shared her confidence.
They could not say with confidence that he would be able to walk again after the accident.
No one can predict with complete confidence what will happen in the financial markets.
She expressed her confidence that they would win.

senses.definition_vi: cảm giác chắc chắn về điều gì đó

senses.definition: a feeling of trust that somebody will keep information private

examples.x: It took a long time to gain her confidence (= make her feel she could trust me).
Eva told me about their relationship in confidence.
This is in the strictest confidence.

senses.definition_vi: cảm giác tin tưởng rằng ai đó sẽ giữ bí mật thông tin

senses.definition: a secret that you tell somebody

examples.x: The girls exchanged confidences.
I could never forgive Mike for betraying a confidence.

senses.definition_vi: một bí mật mà bạn nói với ai đó

senses.definition: to be trusted with somebody’s secrets

examples.x: He is said to be very much in the president's confidence.

senses.definition_vi: được tin cậy với bí mật của ai đó

senses.definition: to tell somebody secrets and personal information about yourself

examples.x: She took me into her confidence and told me about the problems she was facing.
He thought he might take Leo into his confidence.

senses.definition_vi: nói với ai đó những bí mật và thông tin cá nhân về bản thân bạn

senses.definition: feeling sure about your own ability to do things and be successful

examples.x: She was in a relaxed, confident mood.
Beneath his confident and charming exterior lurked a mass of insecurities.
I was actually fairly confident about my chances.
The teacher wants the children to feel confident about asking questions when they don't understand.
He'd learned to be confident in his ability to handle anything life threw at him.

senses.definition_vi: cảm thấy chắc chắn về khả năng của chính bạn để làm mọi việc và thành công

senses.definition: feeling certain that something will happen in the way that you want or expect

examples.x: The Democrats were confident of victory.
The team feels confident of winning.
We are confident about the future.
I'm confident that you will get the job.
He said he remained confident that the dispute could be resolved.
We're pretty confident we can win the case.
She was quietly confident that everything would go as planned.

senses.definition_vi: cảm thấy chắc chắn rằng điều gì đó sẽ xảy ra theo cách bạn muốn hoặc mong đợi

senses.definition: an arrangement of the parts of something or a group of things; the form or shape that this arrangement produces

examples.x: The design is based on four configurations of squares.
There was a changing configuration of lights coming from the stadium.
The stars seemed to appear in a different configuration.

senses.definition_vi: sự sắp xếp các bộ phận của một cái gì đó hoặc một nhóm các thứ; hình thức hoặc hình dạng mà sự sắp xếp này tạo ra

senses.definition: the equipment and programs that form a computer system and the way that these are set up to run

examples.x: Performance will vary depending on your hardware and software configurations.

senses.definition_vi: thiết bị và chương trình tạo nên một hệ thống máy tính và cách chúng được thiết lập để hoạt động

senses.definition: to keep somebody/something inside the limits of a particular activity, subject, area, etc.

examples.x: The work will not be confined to the Glasgow area.
I will confine myself to looking at the period from 1900 to 1916.
Here the river is confined in a narrow channel.

senses.definition_vi: giữ ai đó/điều gì đó trong giới hạn của một hoạt động, chủ đề, khu vực, v.v. cụ thể

senses.definition: to keep a person or an animal in a small or closed space

examples.x: Keep the dog confined in a suitable travelling cage.
The soldiers concerned were confined to barracks (= had to stay in the barracks, as a punishment).

senses.definition_vi: giữ một người hoặc một con vật trong một không gian nhỏ hoặc kín

senses.definition: to have to stay in bed, in a wheelchair, etc.

examples.x: She was confined to bed with the flu.
He was confined to a wheelchair after the accident.

senses.definition_vi: phải ở trên giường, trên xe lăn, v.v.

senses.definition: to state or show that something is definitely true or correct, especially by providing evidence

examples.x: His guilty expression confirmed my suspicions.
to confirm a diagnosis/report
to confirm results/findings
Rumours of job losses were later confirmed.
We have yet to confirm the identities of the victims.
She said she could not confirm or deny the allegations.
The authorities refused to confirm any details.
Police sources confirmed that ten people had been arrested at the march.
A government official confirmed to the newspaper that Britain was pushing hard for an end to the arms embargo.
Can you confirm what happened?
It has been confirmed that an official complaint was made to the council.

senses.definition_vi: khẳng định hoặc chứng tỏ rằng điều gì đó là hoàn toàn đúng hoặc chính xác, đặc biệt là bằng cách cung cấp bằng chứng

senses.definition: to make a position, an agreement, etc. more definite or official; to establish somebody/something clearly

examples.x: Please write to confirm your reservation (= say that it is definite).
After a six-month probationary period, her position was confirmed.
Has everyone confirmed (that) they’re coming?
It has been confirmed that the meeting will take place next week.
He was confirmed as captain for the rest of the season.
I'm very happy to confirm you in your post.

senses.definition_vi: làm cho một vị trí, một thỏa thuận, v.v. trở nên chính thức hoặc rõ ràng hơn; thiết lập ai đó/điều gì đó một cách rõ ràng

senses.definition: to make somebody feel or believe something even more strongly

examples.x: The walk in the mountains confirmed his fear of heights.
This latest tragedy merely confirms my view that the law must be tightened.

senses.definition_vi: làm cho ai đó cảm thấy hoặc tin tưởng điều gì đó mạnh mẽ hơn

senses.definition: to perform the Christian or Jewish ceremony of confirmation

examples.x: She was baptized when she was a month old and confirmed when she was thirteen.

senses.definition_vi: thực hiện nghi lễ Kitô giáo hoặc Do Thái giáo về sự xác nhận

senses.definition: a statement, letter, etc. that shows that something is true, correct or definite

examples.x: I'm still waiting for confirmation of the test results.

senses.definition_vi: một tuyên bố, thư, v.v. cho thấy điều gì đó là đúng, chính xác hoặc chắc chắn

senses.definition: a ceremony at which a person becomes a full member of the Christian Church

examples.x: a confirmation service

senses.definition_vi: một buổi lễ mà một người trở thành thành viên chính thức của Giáo hội Kitô giáo

senses.definition: a Jewish ceremony similar to a bar mitzvah or bat mitzvah but usually for young people over the age of 16
senses.definition_vi: một nghi lễ Do Thái giáo tương tự như bar mitzvah hoặc bat mitzvah nhưng thường dành cho những người trẻ trên 16 tuổi

senses.definition: a situation in which people, groups or countries disagree strongly or are involved in a serious argument

examples.x: The violence was the result of political conflicts.

examples.cf: conflict between A and B (over something)
examples.x: a conflict between two cultures
His task will be to resolve potential conflicts between the British and Scottish governments.
The prime minister wants to avoid conflict with the unions.
The government has done nothing to resolve the conflict over nurses' pay.
She found herself in conflict with her parents over her future career.
John often comes into conflict with his boss.
The terms of the will became a source of conflict within the family.
She has received training in conflict resolution.

senses.definition_vi: nếu hai ý tưởng, niềm tin, câu chuyện, v.v. mâu thuẫn, thì không thể tồn tại cùng nhau hoặc cả hai đều đúng

senses.definition: a violent situation or period of fighting between two countries

examples.x: armed/military conflict
The country has experienced internal conflict over the last decade.
Hopes of ending the conflict in the region are fading.
international efforts to find a peaceful solution to the conflict
This isolated state faces the risk of another violent conflict with its neighbour.
They are engaged in a bloody conflict over the disputed territory.

examples.cf: conflict between A and B (over something)
examples.x: A conflict between the two countries could easily spread across the whole region.

senses.definition_vi: nếu hai ý tưởng, niềm tin, câu chuyện, v.v. mâu thuẫn, thì không thể tồn tại cùng nhau hoặc cả hai đều đúng

senses.definition: a situation in which there are ideas, opinions, feelings or wishes that are opposed to each other; a situation in which it is difficult to choose

examples.x: Her diary was a record of her inner conflict.
The story tells of a classic conflict between love and duty.
Many of these ideas appear to be in conflict with each other.
He faced a conflict of loyalties.
a serious conflict of opinion

senses.definition_vi: nếu hai ý tưởng, niềm tin, câu chuyện, v.v. mâu thuẫn, thì không thể tồn tại cùng nhau hoặc cả hai đều đúng

senses.definition: a situation in which somebody has two jobs, aims, roles, etc. and cannot treat both of them equally and fairly at the same time

examples.x: There was a conflict of interest between his business dealings and his political activities.
One member of the planning committee had a conflict of interest as he lived near the proposed road.
There is often a conflict of interests between farmers and conservationists.

senses.definition_vi: nếu hai ý tưởng, niềm tin, câu chuyện, v.v. mâu thuẫn, thì không thể tồn tại cùng nhau hoặc cả hai đều đúng

senses.definition: to appear and need to be dealt with by somebody

examples.x: What is to be done about the economic problems confronting the country?
I was suddenly confronted by the task of rewriting the entire book.
The government found itself confronted by massive opposition.

senses.definition_vi: xuất hiện và cần được ai đó giải quyết

senses.definition: to deal with a problem or difficult situation

examples.x: She knew that she had to confront her fears.

senses.definition_vi: giải quyết một vấn đề hoặc tình huống khó khăn

senses.definition: to face somebody so that they cannot avoid seeing and hearing you, especially in an unfriendly or dangerous situation

examples.x: This was the first time he had confronted an armed robber.
Confronted by an angry crowd, the police retreated.
The demonstrators found themselves confronted by a line of police, blocking the road.

senses.definition_vi: đối mặt với ai đó để họ không thể tránh khỏi việc nhìn thấy và nghe thấy bạn, đặc biệt là trong một tình huống không thân thiện hoặc nguy hiểm

senses.definition: to make somebody face or deal with an unpleasant or difficult person or situation

examples.x: He confronted her with a choice between her career or their relationship.
These texts constantly confront the reader with their demanding claims.

senses.definition_vi: làm cho ai đó đối mặt hoặc đối phó với một người hoặc tình huống khó chịu hoặc khó khăn

senses.definition: to have something in front of you that you have to deal with or react to

examples.x: Most people when confronted with a horse will pat it.

senses.definition_vi: có điều gì đó ở trước mặt bạn mà bạn phải đối phó hoặc phản ứng

senses.definition: a situation in which there is anger between people or groups who disagree because they have different opinions

examples.x: She wanted to avoid another confrontation with her father.
Confrontation between employers and unions has resulted in strike action.

senses.definition_vi: một tình huống mà có sự tức giận giữa những người hoặc nhóm bất đồng vì họ có những ý kiến khác nhau

senses.definition: to make somebody unable to think clearly or understand something

examples.x: These two sets of statistics are guaranteed to confuse the public.
They confused me with conflicting accounts of what happened.

senses.definition_vi: làm cho ai đó không thể suy nghĩ rõ ràng hoặc hiểu điều gì đó

senses.definition: to think wrongly that somebody/something is somebody/something else

examples.x: People often confuse me and my twin sister.
Be careful not to confuse quantity with quality.
She says that meteors breaking apart can easily be confused for UFOs.

senses.definition_vi: nghĩ sai rằng ai đó/điều gì đó là ai đó/điều gì đó khác

senses.definition: to make a subject more difficult to understand

examples.x: His comments only served to confuse the issue further.

senses.definition_vi: làm cho một chủ đề trở nên khó hiểu hơn

senses.definition: unable to think clearly or to understand what is happening or what somebody is saying

examples.x: I'm confused—say all that again.
I'm getting really confused now. What has that got to do with it?
He was depressed and in a confused state of mind.
a confused look/expression
I was confused about my feelings for him.
People are confused about all the different labels on food these days.
She seemed confused by the question.

senses.definition_vi: không thể suy nghĩ rõ ràng hoặc hiểu những gì đang xảy ra hoặc những gì ai đó đang nói

senses.definition: not clear or easy to understand

examples.x: The children gave a confused account of what had happened.
His mind was crowded with confused thoughts.
A confused situation followed the military coup.

senses.definition_vi: không rõ ràng hoặc khó hiểu

senses.definition: difficult to understand; not clear

examples.x: The instructions on the box are very confusing.
a confusing situation/experience
confusing messages/signals
a confusing array of options
This is where it all starts to get really confusing.
Beginners may find the terminology confusing.
The new signs will be very confusing for tourists.
All this information can be confusing to the user.
The site is somewhat confusing to navigate.

examples.cf: it is confusing (for/to somebody) to do something
examples.x: It would be confusing to have two sets of regulations for a single country.

senses.definition_vi: khó hiểu; không rõ ràng

senses.definition: a state of not being certain about what is happening, what you should do, what something means, etc.

examples.x: The announcement caused a lot of confusion.
There is some confusion about what the correct procedure should be.
There was a confusion as to what to do next.

senses.definition_vi: một trạng thái không chắc chắn về những gì đang xảy ra, những gì bạn nên làm, ý nghĩa của điều gì đó, v.v.

senses.definition: the fact of making a mistake about who somebody is or what something is

examples.x: To avoid confusion, please write the children's names clearly on all their school clothes.
confusion between letters of the alphabet like ‘o’ or ‘a’

senses.definition_vi: việc mắc lỗi về việc ai đó là ai hoặc điều gì đó là gì

senses.definition: a situation in which you feel embarrassed because you do not understand something and are not sure what to do

examples.x: He looked at me in confusion and did not answer the question.
Sacha felt confusion sweeping over her as she read the letter.

senses.definition_vi: một tình huống mà bạn cảm thấy bối rối vì bạn không hiểu điều gì đó và không chắc phải làm gì

senses.definition: a confused situation in which people do not know what action to take

examples.x: Fighting had broken out and all was chaos and confusion.
Her unexpected arrival threw us into total confusion.

senses.definition_vi: một tình huống bối rối mà mọi người không biết phải hành động như thế nào

senses.definition: to tell somebody that you are pleased about their success or achievements

examples.x: I congratulated them all on their results.
The authors are to be congratulated on producing such a clear and authoritative work.

senses.definition_vi: nói với ai đó rằng bạn hài lòng về thành công hoặc thành tích của họ

senses.definition: to feel pleased and proud because you have achieved something or been successful at something

examples.x: You can congratulate yourself on having done an excellent job.
The organizers are congratulating themselves on attracting record numbers to the event.

senses.definition_vi: cảm thấy hài lòng và tự hào vì bạn đã đạt được điều gì đó hoặc thành công trong việc gì đó

senses.definition: a group of people who are gathered together in a church for a religious service, not including the priest and choir

examples.x: The congregation stood to sing the hymn.

senses.definition_vi: một nhóm người tụ tập trong nhà thờ cho một buổi lễ tôn giáo, không bao gồm linh mục và dàn hợp xướng

senses.definition: a group of people who regularly attend a particular church

examples.x: members of local congregations
The congregation is/are very diverse in terms of background and ethnicity.

senses.definition_vi: một nhóm người thường xuyên tham dự một nhà thờ cụ thể

senses.definition: a group or collection of people, animals or things

examples.x: Large congregations of birds filled the evening skies.

senses.definition_vi: một nhóm hoặc tập hợp người, động vật hoặc vật

senses.definition: related to or belonging to a congress or the Congress in the US

examples.x: a congressional committee/bill
the midterm Congressional elections

senses.definition_vi: liên quan đến hoặc thuộc về một quốc hội hoặc Quốc hội ở Hoa Kỳ

senses.definition: to join together two or more things; to be joined together

examples.x: The towns are connected by train and bus services.
The island is connected to the mainland by a bridge.
The canal was built to connect Sheffield with the Humber estuary.
The rooms on this floor connect.
a connecting door (= one that connects two rooms)

senses.definition_vi: nối hai hoặc nhiều thứ lại với nhau; được nối với nhau

senses.definition: to join something to the main supply of electricity, gas, water, etc. or to another piece of equipment

examples.x: We're waiting for the broadband to be connected.
First connect the printer to the computer.

senses.definition_vi: kết nối một cái gì đó với nguồn cung cấp chính về điện, gas, nước, v.v. hoặc với một thiết bị khác

senses.definition: to join a computer or a mobile device to the internet or to a computer network

examples.x: The device can be hooked up to a mobile phone to connect wirelessly.
Click ‘Continue’ to connect to the internet.
My phone keeps refusing to connect to the Wi-Fi.
The system harnesses the processing power of many computers connected by a high-speed network.
Simply connect your device to the camera's Wi-Fi signal.
Many guests leave their laptops connected to the hotel network when they're not in their rooms.

senses.definition_vi: kết nối máy tính hoặc thiết bị di động với internet hoặc mạng máy tính

senses.definition: to notice or make a link between people, things, events, etc.

examples.x: I was surprised to hear them mentioned together: I had never connected them before.
I found it hard to connect the two ideas in my mind.
There was nothing to connect him with the crime.
He made a statement connecting the terrorist group to the attack.

senses.definition_vi: nhận thấy hoặc tạo ra một liên kết giữa mọi người, sự vật, sự kiện, v.v.

senses.definition: to arrive just before another one leaves so that passengers can change from one to the other

examples.x: His flight to Amsterdam connects with an afternoon flight to New York.
There's a connecting flight at noon.

senses.definition_vi: đến ngay trước khi một chuyến khác rời đi để hành khách có thể đổi từ chuyến này sang chuyến khác

senses.definition: to put somebody in contact by phone

examples.x: After a long wait I was connected to customer services.

senses.definition_vi: liên lạc với ai đó qua điện thoại

senses.definition: to form a good relationship with somebody so that you like and understand each other

examples.x: They met a couple of times but they didn't really connect.

senses.definition_vi: hình thành mối quan hệ tốt đẹp với ai đó để bạn thích và hiểu nhau

senses.definition: to hit somebody/something

examples.x: The blow connected and she felt a surge of pain.

senses.definition_vi: đánh ai đó/cái gì đó

senses.definition: (of two or more things or people) having a link between them

examples.x: We do not believe that the incidents are connected.
The two issues are closely connected.
market prices and other connected matters
The fall in retail sales is directly connected with the decline in employment.
jobs connected with the environment
Many computer files connected to the case have been erased.
They are connected by marriage.

senses.definition_vi: (của hai hoặc nhiều thứ hoặc người) có một liên kết giữa chúng

senses.definition: something that connects two facts, ideas, etc.

examples.x: Scientists have established a connection between cholesterol levels and heart disease.
a direct/close/strong connection with something
His resignation must have some connection with the recent scandal.
Consumers are more likely to buy something from a person or shop they feel a personal connection to.
How did you make the connection (= realize that there was a connection between two facts that did not seem to be related)?

senses.definition_vi: một cái gì đó kết nối hai sự kiện, ý tưởng, v.v.

senses.definition: the act of connecting or the state of being connected

examples.x: a broadband/wireless/Wi-Fi/network connection
I'm having problems with my internet connection.
Connection to the gas supply was delayed for three days.

senses.definition_vi: hành động kết nối hoặc trạng thái được kết nối

senses.definition: a point, especially in an electrical system, where two parts connect

examples.x: A faulty connection caused the machine to stop.
